s: diploma (higher education only, e.g., Master’s degree).
Diplom.et: Borrowed from Latin diploma. First attested in the 17th century.

diploid.et: From diplo- + -id. Coined in the second half of the 19th century by botanist Eduard Strasburger.

s: A German university degree which is awarded to students of economics. It is comparable to a master's degree.

diplomatisch.et: First attested in the 18th century. By surface analysis, Diplom + -at- + -isch.

s: diphtheria (infectious disease of the upper respiratory tract)

Dipsomane.et: Based on Ancient Greek δίψα (dípsa, “thirst”) + μανία (manía).

s: An engineer's degree given in several countries. (replaced by the Bologna process by Bachelor of Engineering and Master of Engineering)
An engineer's degree given to females in Austria till 2008.
Diplomingenieurin.et: From Diplom + Ingenieurin, or rather Diplomingenieur + -in.

Diptychon.et: From Ancient Greek δίπτυχον (díptukhon), neuter singular of δίπτυχος (díptukhos).

s: a major district town in w:Sächsische Schweiz-Osterzgebirge district, Saxony
Dippoldiswalde.et: First mentioned as Dipoldiswale in 1218. The first element is a variant of the given name Dietbold; the second element is from Wald (“forest”).

s: a native or inhabitant of Dippoldiswalde

在西方，主要是在威尼斯使节报告的影响下（外交行家们怀着热情阅读这些报告），外交在查理五世的时代——马基雅维利的时代——首先成为一门被有意识地培养的艺术；它的行家大多受过人文主义教育，彼此把对方看作一个受过训练的内行圈子，类似于中国战国时代受过人文教育的政治家。
